description.html: The terracotta-colored skull gives a terrarium a striking, slightly wild look. The wide-open jaw, pronounced teeth and deep eye sockets make it look as if it had lain in desert sand for years. The warm reddish-brown color goes well with sandy and clay substrates, stones and dry branches, so it suits desert and semi-desert setups especially well.

The skull is primarily an ornament, but reptiles and spiders often explore it, climb over it or rest next to it. Still provide a separate hide, because every animal needs an enclosed spot where it feels safe.

Before placing it, wash the skull in lukewarm water, without detergents or chemicals whose residue your animal could lick. Set it on a firm base or bury it slightly so it does not tip over when the animal climbs on it. During routine terrarium cleaning, take it out, rinse it and brush substrate and waste out of the crevices. You will find more decorations among our terrarium supplies.
